01-dart.title: Dart foundations and object-oriented programming
01-dart.prerequisites: Programming logic, functions and control flow.
01-dart.objectives: Work with types, null safety, collections, functions and classes. Model rules independently of the user interface.
01-dart.activity: Build a small terminal inventory in your own study repository. Separate data from commands and handle invalid input.
01-dart.note: Use Masmorra ASCII as a parallel learning path: study foundations and object-oriented programming before the advanced stages. The game uses a terminal rather than Flutter widgets. Use the current version of the chosen repository, synthetic data and its documented validation steps. Record the environment and distinguish real execution, emulation and a local demonstration. These activities are proposals for your own study repository.
01-dart.reading: Masmorra ASCII: start with the foundations and object-oriented programming in the terminal.

exercises.title: Types and validation
exercises.objective: Accept an item name and quantity.
exercises.criteria: Reject an empty name and a negative quantity without terminating the program.

exercises.title: Collections
exercises.objective: Add items and look them up by name.
exercises.criteria: Demonstrate an empty collection, a successful search and a search with no result.

exercises.title: Classes
exercises.objective: Represent an item as a typed value.
exercises.criteria: Make invalid construction impossible or reject it explicitly.

exercises.title: Null safety
exercises.objective: Model a lookup that might not find an item.
exercises.criteria: Handle absence without using a non-null assertion to ignore it.

exercises.title: Tests
exercises.objective: Verify the inventory rules.
exercises.criteria: Provide independent tests for adding items, looking them up and rejecting invalid data.

02-forms.title: Forms and validation
02-forms.objectives: Separate fields, input conversion and calculation rules. Provide useful messages and reproducible results.
02-forms.activity: Choose a calculator, run its current workflow and add a validation case with a test. Use the rules and units documented by the chosen case study.
02-forms.note: The calculators represent different domains. Do not transfer a formula or rounding rule from one to another without a reason. Use the current version of the chosen repository, synthetic data and its documented validation steps. Record the environment and distinguish real execution, emulation and a local demonstration. These activities are proposals for your own study repository.
02-forms.reading: A Ordem do Código Limpo: discuss understandable names and rules when reviewing the form.

exercises.title: Required fields
exercises.objective: Validate an empty form.
exercises.criteria: Display errors next to the fields without producing a fabricated result.

exercises.title: Conversion
exercises.objective: Define the accepted numeric input.
exercises.criteria: Demonstrate the decimal separator, invalid text and the documented behavior.

exercises.title: Units
exercises.objective: Make the quantities and units explicit.
exercises.criteria: Use consistent labels and results, with a test based on an independently calculated value.

exercises.title: An isolated rule
exercises.objective: Extract a calculation from the interface.
exercises.criteria: Test the rule without initializing widgets.

exercises.title: Interaction
exercises.objective: Verify the complete form.
exercises.criteria: Provide a widget test that fills the fields, calculates a result and covers at least one correction after an error.

03-layouts.title: Layouts and interaction
03-layouts.objectives: Build a visual hierarchy, interaction states and adaptive layouts. Keep business rules separate from presentation.
03-layouts.activity: Choose a case study and review its workflow on a narrow screen, a wide screen and with keyboard navigation.
03-layouts.note: Game rules and mathematical operations belong to the domain. Visual changes should preserve existing results. Use the current version of the chosen repository, synthetic data and its documented validation steps. Record the environment and distinguish real execution, emulation and a local demonstration. These activities are proposals for your own study repository.
03-layouts.reading: A Ordem do Código Limpo: relate implementation clarity to interaction decisions.

exercises.title: Responsive layouts
exercises.objective: Adapt a screen to two widths.
exercises.criteria: Keep every essential action accessible and avoid clipped content.

exercises.title: Semantics
exercises.objective: Identify controls for assistive technologies.
exercises.criteria: Give actions useful names instead of using unlabeled icons.

exercises.title: Focus
exercises.objective: Complete a workflow using the keyboard.
exercises.criteria: Provide a predictable focus order and visible activation.

exercises.title: State
exercises.objective: Preserve a game or calculation when the layout changes.
exercises.criteria: Demonstrate in a test that the data remains available.

exercises.title: Feedback
exercises.objective: Communicate an invalid action.
exercises.criteria: Show an understandable message and leave the interface ready for another attempt.

04-apis.title: HTTP APIs and asynchronous state
04-apis.objectives: Consume external data, parse JSON at the boundary and distinguish loading, empty, success and error states.
04-apis.activity: Choose a query and implement a reproducible error response. Use a replaceable client in tests so they do not depend on an external network.
04-apis.note: The current application implementation determines the API and libraries in use. An old article title does not establish that DIO or Google Sheets remains the active integration. Use the current version of the chosen repository, synthetic data and its documented validation steps. Record the environment and distinguish real execution, emulation and a local demonstration. These activities are proposals for your own study repository.
04-apis.reading:
A Agência Holística de Depuração: use the reading as a starting point for investigating integration failures.

[Agência Holística · Volume II — Tudo Tem Memória](https://kleberandrade.dev/books/agencia-vol-2): Use the reading to investigate an integration failure with logs and a reproducible sequence.

[Agência Holística · Volume III — A Conta Que Ficou](https://kleberandrade.dev/books/agencia-vol-3): Discuss retries and idempotency: a test with a simulated client should check whether a retry duplicates an effect.

exercises.title: States
exercises.objective: Represent loading, an empty response and a result.
exercises.criteria: Demonstrate each state with controlled data.

exercises.title: Parsing
exercises.objective: Validate an unexpected response.
exercises.criteria: Handle invalid JSON or a missing field as a controlled error.

exercises.title: Failures
exercises.objective: Handle a timeout or an unavailable service.
exercises.criteria: Show a message and allow another attempt without inventing successful data.

exercises.title: Concurrency
exercises.objective: Prevent an old result from replacing the latest query.
exercises.criteria: Provide a test that controls the order of two responses.

exercises.title: A contract
exercises.objective: Document a query.
exercises.criteria: Describe its input, output and limits, and run tests with synthetic fixtures.

05-local-data.title: Local persistence
05-local-data.objectives: Persist data, reconstruct state after restarting and handle changes to the stored format.
05-local-data.activity: Create a record, close the application and open it again. Document the storage mechanism actually used by the current version.
05-local-data.note: SQLite, Sembast and Hive appear in historical article titles. The current README and code determine the storage mechanism and platform compatibility. Use the current version of the chosen repository, synthetic data and its documented validation steps. Record the environment and distinguish real execution, emulation and a local demonstration. These activities are proposals for your own study repository.
05-local-data.reading:
Masmorra ASCII and A Agência Holística de Depuração: compare persistence and failure investigation with the chosen application.

[Agência Holística · Volume II — Tudo Tem Memória](https://kleberandrade.dev/books/agencia-vol-2): Compare displayed state with stored state and record how to detect an inconsistency.

[Agência Holística · Volume III — A Conta Que Ficou](https://kleberandrade.dev/books/agencia-vol-3): Connect the reading to a restoration test: recover a sample and check its data, rather than only the existence of a file.

exercises.title: Reopening
exercises.objective: Preserve a record between sessions.
exercises.criteria: Demonstrate creation, restarting and reading the same content.

exercises.title: Updating
exercises.objective: Edit and delete a record.
exercises.criteria: Keep the changes correct after reopening the application.

exercises.title: The format
exercises.objective: Define behavior for invalid stored data.
exercises.criteria: Reproduce the case in a test and avoid silent data loss.

exercises.title: Evolution
exercises.objective: Change the schema using an explicit strategy.
exercises.criteria: Keep a sample of the earlier format readable or apply a tested migration.

exercises.title: Isolation
exercises.objective: Test the repository with temporary storage.
exercises.criteria: Ensure that two runs do not accidentally share data.

06-services.title: External services and machine learning
06-services.prerequisites: Module 4 and an understanding of asynchronous operations.
06-services.objectives: Separate the interface from the integration. Communicate configuration requirements, failures and prediction limits.
06-services.activity: Run a case study in its documented mode and identify real integration, fixtures and demonstration mode.
06-services.note: OCR/ML Kit remains a historical topic without a linked tutorial in this course. A classifier does not by itself establish use of a particular service or model. Use the current version of the chosen repository, synthetic data and its documented validation steps. Record the environment and distinguish real execution, emulation and a local demonstration. These activities are proposals for your own study repository.
06-services.reading:
O Último Sprint da Humanidade: discuss who validates results and code produced with automation.

[Agência Holística · Volume III — A Conta Que Ficou](https://kleberandrade.dev/books/agencia-vol-3): Discuss model drift and input validation when comparing the results of an integration or classifier.

exercises.title: Configuration
exercises.objective: Separate public parameters from secrets.
exercises.criteria: Document a test run without committing credentials.

exercises.title: An adapter
exercises.objective: Replace the service with a test double.
exercises.criteria: Test the interface workflow without a real service call.

exercises.title: External failure
exercises.objective: Handle an unavailable service.
exercises.criteria: Report the failure without presenting a simulated response as a real one.

exercises.title: Limits
exercises.objective: Explain the integration output.
exercises.criteria: Distinguish the response, confidence when available and cases outside the scope.

exercises.title: Evidence
exercises.objective: Record a reproducible run.
exercises.criteria: Identify the synthetic input, execution mode, result and observed limitations.

07-firebase.title: Firebase and authentication
07-firebase.prerequisites: Modules 4 and 5, and separation of data interfaces.
07-firebase.objectives: Understand sessions, authorization, remote persistence and access-rule testing.
07-firebase.activity: Choose an application and identify its documented local and Firebase workflows. Use emulators when configured; production accounts are not prerequisites for the interface exercises.
07-firebase.note: The sign-in methods in the 2019–2020 index provide historical context. Phone, Google or password sign-in should only be presented as available when the current version implements and documents it. Use the current version of the chosen repository, synthetic data and its documented validation steps. Record the environment and distinguish real execution, emulation and a local demonstration. These activities are proposals for your own study repository.
07-firebase.reading: A Guerra das Arquiteturas: discuss boundaries between identity, access rules and storage.

exercises.title: Sessions
exercises.objective: Model signing in, signing out and an expired session.
exercises.criteria: Cover all three states in tests using test data.

exercises.title: Authorization
exercises.objective: Define who may edit a record.
exercises.criteria: Provide a rule or policy test that denies access to a different user.

exercises.title: Persistence
exercises.objective: Separate local and remote implementations.
exercises.criteria: Provide a common contract and identify the execution mode in the interface or documentation.

exercises.title: Errors
exercises.objective: Handle a failed write.
exercises.criteria: Report the error and avoid confirming success prematurely.

exercises.title: Configuration
exercises.objective: Reproduce the test environment.
exercises.criteria: Provide instructions without secrets and evidence of executed tests, distinguishing the emulator from production.

08-iot.title: Internet of Things
08-iot.prerequisites: Module 4 and basic messaging and connection concepts.
08-iot.objectives: Understand protocols, serialization, connection state and the boundary between simulation and hardware.
08-iot.activity: Explore a documented MQTT or Bluetooth workflow. Start with a simulated transport and only test hardware when its specific requirements are met.
08-iot.note: Bluetooth and Arduino require a compatible platform and equipment. The old Twilio/SMS topic has no linked tutorial here and does not authorize sending messages. Use the current version of the chosen repository, synthetic data and its documented validation steps. Record the environment and distinguish real execution, emulation and a local demonstration. These activities are proposals for your own study repository.
08-iot.reading: A Guerra das Arquiteturas: discuss responsibilities across the application, transport and device.

exercises.title: Messages
exercises.objective: Define a command contract.
exercises.criteria: Document the unit, range and rejection of invalid messages.

exercises.title: Connections
exercises.objective: Represent disconnection and reconnection.
exercises.criteria: Demonstrate transitions in a test without claiming a connection that does not exist.

exercises.title: Simulation
exercises.objective: Replace the transport.
exercises.criteria: Run a command in a hardware-free test and label that execution mode.

exercises.title: Limits
exercises.objective: Handle commands outside the allowed range or without authorization.
exercises.criteria: Demonstrate rejection at the relevant boundary in a test.

exercises.title: Platforms
exercises.objective: Document a run.
exercises.criteria: List the equipment, operating system and protocol actually tested, without treating a web test as proof of real radio operation.

09-architecture.title: Architecture and maintenance
09-architecture.prerequisites: Modules 1 through 5 and a case study already run.
09-architecture.objectives: Set boundaries between domain, interface and infrastructure. Choose abstractions based on the required behavior.
09-architecture.activity: Use an application from an earlier module to isolate a rule from the interface. Compare it with a design pattern only when the problem justifies doing so.
09-architecture.note: O Grimório dos Padrões provides TypeScript examples: study the concepts and implement your activity in Dart. MVC, MVVM, MVP and Clean Architecture are study alternatives, not guaranteed code modules in this index. Use the current version of the chosen repository, synthetic data and its documented validation steps. Record the environment and distinguish real execution, emulation and a local demonstration. These activities are proposals for your own study repository.
09-architecture.reading:
O Grimório dos Padrões, Fantasia Técnica and Masmorra ASCII: compare concepts and apply only those needed by the case study.

[Agência Holística · Volume II — Tudo Tem Memória](https://kleberandrade.dev/books/agencia-vol-2): Use a reading case to discuss flaky tests, observability and the boundaries where a failure should be investigated.

exercises.title: Responsibilities
exercises.objective: Draw a dependency map for the chosen case study.
exercises.criteria: Explain which modules know about the interface, domain and storage.

exercises.title: A rule
exercises.objective: Isolate a business decision.
exercises.criteria: Call the rule in tests without a UI framework.

exercises.title: Infrastructure
exercises.objective: Replace data access through a contract.
exercises.criteria: Use an alternative implementation in a test without changing the rule.

exercises.title: Refactoring
exercises.objective: Improve the structure while preserving behavior.
exercises.criteria: Show tests before and after the change and explain the reduction in complexity.

exercises.title: A decision
exercises.objective: Record an architectural choice.
exercises.criteria: Compare an alternative and make the context, consequences and limits of the decision explicit.

10-final-project.title: Complete applications and final assignment
10-final-project.prerequisites: Earlier modules relevant to the chosen domain.
10-final-project.objectives: Integrate the interface, data, tests, documentation and execution evidence within an achievable scope.
10-final-project.activity: Choose a domain, define a small workflow and deliver a reproducible version with synthetic data. The module 7 applications are additional options.
10-final-project.note: The goal is a verifiable delivery. Health information or production formulas require sources and domain limits; an academic demonstration is not clinical or chemical validation. Use the current version of the chosen repository, synthetic data and its documented validation steps. Record the environment and distinguish real execution, emulation and a local demonstration. These activities are proposals for your own study repository.
10-final-project.reading:
Fantasia Ágil and the author’s catalog: use the readings to discuss scope, acceptance criteria and responsibility for delivery.

[Agência Holística · Volume III — A Conta Que Ficou](https://kleberandrade.dev/books/agencia-vol-3): Include a reliability acceptance criterion in the delivery: a reproducible failure, data recovery or rejection of a duplicate operation.

exercises.title: Scope
exercises.objective: Define a user journey and acceptance criteria.
exercises.criteria: List the main workflow, one relevant error and what is outside the delivery scope.

exercises.title: Implementation
exercises.objective: Complete the journey with synthetic data.
exercises.criteria: Demonstrate the interface and persistence or an identified integration from end to end.

exercises.title: Quality
exercises.objective: Verify critical decisions and interactions.
exercises.criteria: Pass relevant tests and provide instructions for reproducing them.

exercises.title: Documentation
exercises.objective: Prepare the delivery README.
exercises.criteria: Include configuration, versions, licensing and credits, real screenshots and observed limits.

exercises.title: Demonstration
exercises.objective: Reproduce the delivery in a clean environment.
exercises.criteria: Run the documented steps and record the outcome, remaining work and a retrospective.

guide.title: Study guide
guide.intro: Course by Prof. Kleber de Oliveira Andrade, Fatec Americana, for the Systems Analysis and Development program. Start with Dart, follow the modules and build on the current case-study repositories.

sections.title: Prepare your environment
paragraphs: Programming logic, functions, conditions and loops help you follow the course. Start with Dart before moving to Flutter interfaces.

Use the [official Flutter installation guide](https://docs.flutter.dev/install) for your operating system and target platform, together with the [initial learning path](https://docs.flutter.dev/learn/pathway). Identify your environment with `flutter --version`, `dart --version` and `flutter doctor -v`.

These commands do not install dependencies for this course index. Address the requirements of your chosen platform. License acceptance and account setup remain decisions for the person preparing the environment.

Open the repository of your chosen case study and follow its current README. Check `pubspec.yaml`, the lockfile, test commands and supported platforms. Do not run `flutter pub get` at the root of this course index or replace a modernized project’s versions with those from historical tutorials.

sections.title: Follow the learning path
paragraphs: Follow the ten modules: Dart; forms; layouts; APIs; local data; services; Firebase; IoT; architecture; and the final assignment. Revisit architecture throughout the activities rather than leaving it until the end.
[Masmorra ASCII](https://masmorra.io/) provides a parallel path for practicing Dart in the terminal. The suggested books connect this path with the course topics.
This repository does not define an official timetable or number of teaching hours. The instructor adapts the activities and service or hardware requirements to the class.

sections.title: Work through each module
paragraphs: Read the objectives, run a documented workflow in a case study and record your environment. Make a small change using synthetic data and verify the result. Every module ends with five exercises: their criteria describe expected evidence, not an answer key or an automated grading service.

In your own delivery repository, record what changed, why, the tests executed and the remaining limitations. Include real screenshots and credit authors and sources. Do not upload passwords, tokens, service-account files or personal data.

sections.title: Completion criteria
paragraphs: A browser test does not prove Bluetooth or camera operation or publication in an application store. Local modes in modernized projects should not be confused with production integrations. Use documented configuration and emulators to test external services.
bullets: Demonstrate the main workflow and at least one invalid case.
Separate rules from the interface and test relevant decisions.
Explain loading, error and empty-data states when applicable.
Record versions and real steps for reproducing the run.
Identify fixtures, simulations, emulators and real integrations.

books.title: Books and learning sites
books.intro: Suggested readings by Kleber de Oliveira Andrade, connected to the course modules. These are teaching suggestions rather than required purchases. Narrative books support discussion; the technical documentation remains the reference for APIs. Use the official pages for availability and formats.

sections.title: Masmorra ASCII · practice Dart
paragraphs: Masmorra ASCII teaches Dart through a terminal roguelike, with 37 chapters and code for each stage. Start with the beginner guide, then explore the contents, chapter examples and concept map.

Suggested connections: module 1 for foundations, null safety, collections and object-oriented programming; module 5 for comparing the game’s JSON persistence with application storage; module 9 for organization, tests, patterns and state machines; and module 10 for planning small, verifiable deliveries.
The game is a terminal activity. Compare concepts and rules before adapting them to a Flutter interface; this course site does not execute or republish the game code.

sections.title: Debugging and discussing systems
paragraphs: Use the reading as a starting point for discussing failure investigation and connections in modules 4, 5 and 9. Compare a reading situation with a reproducible failure in your case study without assuming that it maps to a specific API.

resources.title: Current references
resources.intro: Use current official documentation to prepare your environment and verify APIs. Compare historical articles with the current case-study code. The 2019–2020 articles remain in the historical index. Some use shortened links, earlier versions or services that have changed. This reorganization does not modify or certify external content.
